verses.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.

xrefs.text: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father and mother and does not listen to them when disciplined,
Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must keep My Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

notes.note: The command in verse one is plural. Then in verses two and three Paul quotes from the law of Moses. Moses was talking to the people of Israel as though they were one person, so your and you are singular there. If that does not make sense, you may need to translate them as plurals.

Paul continues to explain how Christians, people who live in the Lord, are to submit themselves to each other. He gives instructions to children, fathers, workers, and masters. Alternate translation: [because you belong to the Lord] or [as followers of the Lord]

The connecting word for introduces the reason of a reason-result relationship. The reason is that children should do what is right. The result is that children should obey their parents. Use a phrase in your language that connects a reason to a result.

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: “Honor your father and mother (which is the first commandment with a promise),

xrefs.text: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
‘Cursed is he who dishonors his father or mother.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.

“A son honors his father, and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is your fear of Me?” says the LORD of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. “But you ask, ‘How have we despised Your name?’
Father and mother are treated with contempt. Within your walls the foreign resident is exploited, the fatherless and the widow are oppressed.

Then Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites: “This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘Because you have obeyed the command of your forefather Jonadab and have kept all his commandments and have done all that he charged you to do,
He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.

verses.text: “that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth.”

xrefs.text: Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

Keep His statutes and commandments, which I am giving you today, so that you and your children after you may prosper, and that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time.

Be careful to obey all these things I command you, so that it may always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
Whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God!”
Hear, O Israel, and be careful to observe them, so that you may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.
Do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD your God swore to give your fathers,

notes.note: The connecting phrase so that introduces a goal relationship. The goal or purpose of obeying your father and mother is to live well and long on the earth.

verses.text: Fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath; instead, bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.

xrefs.text: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.

notes.note: Alternate translation: [do not make your children angry] or [do not cause your children to be angry]
The connecting word Instead introduces a contrast relationship. Fathers provoking their children to anger is in contrast to raising their children in discipline and instruction.

notes.quote: ἐκτρέφετε αὐτὰ ἐν παιδείᾳ καὶ νουθεσίᾳ Κυρίου
notes.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the words discipline and instruction, you could express the same ideas with verbal forms. Alternate translation: [teach them to become adults by making sure that they know and do what the Lord wants them to do]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear and sincerity of heart, just as you would obey Christ.

xrefs.text: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.
Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not argumentative,
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name.

“A son honors his father, and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is your fear of Me?” says the LORD of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. “But you ask, ‘How have we despised Your name?’
Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.

notes.note: The phrase fear and trembling uses two similar ideas to emphasize the importance of honoring their masters. Alternate translation: [with deep respect]
Here, trembling is an exaggeration used to emphasize how important it is that slaves obey their masters. Alternate translation: [and deep respect] or [as though you were shaking with fear]
Here, heart is a metonym for a person’s mind or intentions. Alternate translation: [with honesty] or [with sincerity]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word honesty, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [honestly] or [sincerely]
To make the meaning of this phrase clear, you may want to include the verb here: “as you obey Christ.”

verses.text: And do this not only to please them while they are watching, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from your heart.

xrefs.text: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
Instead, we speak as those approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, not in order to please men but God, who examines our hearts.
Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord’s will is.
Consequently, he does not live out his remaining time on earth for human passions, but for the will of God.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.
Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.

notes.note: The connecting word but introduces a contrast relationship. Obeying our masters as men-pleasers is in contrast to obeying them because we are slaves of Christ.
Alternate translation: [as though your earthly master were Christ himself]
Here, soul is a metonym for “attitudes” or “intentions.” Alternate translation: [wholeheartedly] or [enthusiastically]

verses.text: Serve with good will, as to the Lord and not to men,

xrefs.text: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, as for the Lord and not for men,
So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear and sincerity of heart, just as you would obey Christ.

Naaman’s servants, however, approached him and said, “My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?”
I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.
At this time the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken a young girl from the land of Israel, and she was serving Naaman’s wife.
You know that I have served your father with all my strength.

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: because you know that the Lord will reward each one for whatever good he does, whether he is slave or free.

xrefs.text: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.
The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.
so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: And masters, do the same for your slaves. Give up your use of threats, because you know that He who is both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no favoritism with Him.

xrefs.text: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
For God does not show favoritism.
If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, showing no partiality and accepting no bribe.
In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.
Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns.

notes.note: Here, the same refers back to “if he does something good” from (Ephesians 6:8). Alternate translation: [you also must treat your slaves well] or [just as slaves must do good to their masters, you also must do good to your slaves]

notes.quote: εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ αὐτῶν καὶ ὑμῶν ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανοῖς
notes.note: Alternate translation: [You know that Christ is the Master of both slaves and their masters, and that he is in heaven]
Alternate translation: [he judges everyone the same way]

verses.text: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.

xrefs.text: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.
being strengthened with all power according to His glorious might so that you may have full endurance and patience, and joyfully
But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness. Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe. These are in accordance with the working of His mighty strength,

notes.note: Paul is using the word translated Finally to introduce a new event in the story. Here Paul gives instructions to make believers strong in this battle we are in for God. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [In conclusion]

These two words, force and strength, are very similar in meaning. Together, they reinforce each other. See how you translated this phrase near the end of Ephesians 1:19. Alternate translation: [his great power]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God

verses.text: Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil’s schemes.

xrefs.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
Then we will no longer be infants, tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching and by the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming.
Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.

notes.quote: ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι ὑμᾶς στῆναι πρὸς τὰς μεθοδίας τοῦ διαβόλου
notes.note: In this metaphor, Paul pictures the spiritual resources that God gives to all Christians as a soldier’s armor. Alternate translation: [Just as a soldier puts on armor to protect himself from enemy attacks, use all of God’s resources to stand firmly against the devil]
Alternate translation: [the tricky plans]

verses.text: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world’s darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.

xrefs.text: He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son,
The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
in which you used to walk when you conformed to the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience.
And having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross.

to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.
far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in the present age but also in the one to come.
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

notes.note: The connecting word For introduces the reason of this reason-result relationship. The reason is that we are in a struggle against spiritual forces of darkness. The result is that we should put on the whole armor of God. Use a phrase in your language that connects a reason to a result.
This expression refers to people, not to spirits who do not have human bodies. Alternate translation: [human beings]
The connecting word but introduces a contrast relationship. People made of flesh and blood are in contrast to spiritual forces.

Here it is implied that the world-controllers refers to powerful spiritual beings. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [against the powerful spiritual beings that rule over people]
Here, darkness is a metaphor for things that are evil. Alternate translation: [during this present evil time]

verses.text: Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand.

xrefs.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil’s schemes.
redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Because you have kept My command to persevere, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
But who can endure the day of His coming? And who can stand when He appears? For He will be like a refiner’s fire, like a launderer’s soap.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.

notes.quote: διὰ τοῦτο, ἀναλάβετε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
notes.note: Christians should use the protective resources God gives them in fighting the devil in the same way that a soldier puts on armor to protect himself against his enemies.

The connecting phrase Because of this introduces the result of a reason-result relationship. The reason is that we are in a battle against evil spiritual forces. The result is that we should put on the whole armor of God. Use a phrase in your language that connects a reason to a result.

notes.quote: ἵνα δυνηθῆτε ἀντιστῆναι ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πονηρᾷ
notes.note: The word withstand means to successfully resist something. Alternate translation: [so that you may be able to resist when evil attacks you]
It may be helpful to state explicitly what believers are to withstand. Alternate translation: [so that you may be able to withstand the attacks of the devil]
The connecting phrase so that introduces a goal relationship. The goal or purpose of putting on the whole armor of God is to be able to withstand the attacks of the spiritual forces of darkness.

verses.text: Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed,

xrefs.text: He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist.
Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober-minded. Set your hope fully on the grace to be given you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth.

Now the horses and riders in my vision looked like this: The riders had breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire, and sulfur. The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths proceeded fire, smoke, and sulfur.

notes.note: The word Stand represents taking a position on what is right and true and successfully resisting forces that try to make the believer compromise that position. See how you translated “stand firm” in Ephesians 6:13. Alternate translation: [So resist evil]

The connecting word therefore introduces the result of a reason-result relationship. The reason is that we believers have put on our spiritual armor. The result is that we will stand and resist the evil spiritual forces. Use a phrase in your language that connects a reason to a result.

notes.quote: περιζωσάμενοι τὴν ὀσφὺν ὑμῶν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ
notes.note: In this metaphor, truth is compared to a soldier’s belt. Truth holds everything together for a believer just as a belt holds the clothing of a soldier together. Alternate translation: [having wrapped yourself in all that is true]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word truth, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [what is true]

In this metaphor, righteousness is compared to a soldier’s breastplate. Just as soldiers put on a breastplate to protect themselves from enemy attacks, believers should behave in a righteous way to protect themselves from spiritual attacks.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word righteousness, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [the right way to live]

verses.text: and with your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace.

xrefs.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
GOD the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer; He makes me walk upon the heights! For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments.
But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.

notes.quote: ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης
notes.note: In this metaphor, the gospel of peace is compared to a soldier’s sandals. Just as a soldier wears sturdy footwear to give him solid footing and enable him to march long distances, the believer must have solid knowledge of the gospel of peace and be ready to go where the Lord sends him to proclaim it.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word peace, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [that makes everything good between people and God]

verses.text: In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.

xrefs.text: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
because everyone born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.”
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.

notes.quote: ἐν πᾶσιν ἀναλαβόντες τὸν θυρεὸν τῆς πίστεως
notes.note: In this metaphor, faith is compared to a soldier’s shield. Just as a soldier uses a shield to protect himself from enemy attacks, the believer must use the faith that God gives for protection when the devil attacks.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word faith, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [that represents how much you trust in the Lord]
The attacks of the devil against a believer are like flaming arrows shot at a soldier by an enemy.

verses.text: And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

xrefs.text: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal.
And from His mouth proceeds a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and He will rule them with an iron scepter. He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
He made My mouth like a sharp sword; He hid Me in the shadow of His hand. He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver.
“Away from Me, Satan! Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’
Therefore repent! Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth.
Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.

notes.note: The salvation that God gives protects the believer’s mind just as a helmet protects the head of a soldier.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word salvation, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [that represents the fact that God has saved you]

notes.quote: τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ Πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ῥῆμα Θεοῦ
notes.note: In this metaphor, God’s message is compared to a soldier’s sword. Just as soldiers use a sword to fight and defeat their enemy, so a believer can use God’s message in the Bible to fight against the devil.

verses.text: Pray in the Spirit at all times, with every kind of prayer and petition. To this end, stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers for all the saints.

xrefs.text: Pray without ceasing.
Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,
Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone —
But you, beloved, by building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit,
In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.
So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.

notes.quote: διὰ πάσης προσευχῆς καὶ δεήσεως, προσευχόμενοι ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ ἐν Πνεύματι
notes.note: Alternate translation: [Pray at all times in the Spirit as you pray and make specific requests]

The connecting phrase to this {end} marks a goal or purpose relationship. The goal is what was just mentioned: to pray at all times in the Spirit. In order to do that, believers must be watchful and persevere in making requests for all the saints. Alternate translation: [for this reason] or [in order to do that]

notes.quote: ἀγρυπνοῦντες ἐν πάσῃ προσκαρτερήσει καὶ δεήσει περὶ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων
notes.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word perseverance, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [persevere in being alert, and pray for all God’s holy people] or [pray with constant alertness for all the believers]

verses.text: Pray also for me, that whenever I open my mouth, words may be given me so that I will boldly make known the mystery of the gospel,

xrefs.text: as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
And now, Lord, consider their threats, and enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness,
Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor, just as it was with you.
Brothers, pray for us as well.
Pray for us; we are convinced that we have a clear conscience and desire to live honorably in every way.
After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.
As you are aware, we had already endured suffering and shameful treatment in Philippi. But in the face of strong opposition, we were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God.
Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

notes.note: Paul is leaving out a word that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete.
